draft.title: The ATP-PC system
card: Muscles hold a small store of ATP and another chemical called phosphocreatine (PC). When ATP is used up, PC breaks down and releases energy to remake ATP.
This system gives energy fastest of the three energy systems. It needs no oxygen and has very few steps.
The store of PC is small, so the system supplies most of the energy for only about 10 seconds of all-out effort.
It suits very short, explosive efforts, such as a sprint start, a shot put throw or a single jump.
draft.remember: ATP-PC is the fastest system, but its small PC store lasts only about 10 seconds.

a.q: Why can the ATP-PC system supply energy for only about 10 seconds of all-out effort?
opts: The muscles hold only a small store of PC
The system needs oxygen, which runs out quickly
The system is too slow to keep up with the effort
Muscles stop making ATP after about 10 seconds
a.why: PC is stored in small amounts, so it is used up fast during all-out effort. The system does not need oxygen, so a lack of oxygen is not the reason it runs out.
a.clue: Think about how much PC the muscles hold.

b.q: Jess is a volleyball player. She leaps once to spike the ball, which takes about one second. Which system gives most of the energy for the jump?
opts: ATP-PC system
Aerobic system
Anaerobic glycolysis system
None, because muscles do not store ATP
b.why: The jump is very short and explosive, and needs energy at once. The ATP-PC system is the fastest, so it supplies most of it. The aerobic system is too slow to start for an effort this brief.
b.clue: Which system is fastest for a one-second effort?

a.best: The muscles hold only a small store of PC

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about how much PC the muscles hold' points straight at the right option, so a student can pick it without understanding why the system runs out.
